reason: Distinguish saved oracle A/C selection rules and the two-case readiness difference; retain B/heuristic results.
before: A gold-schema top-ten oracle yields 270 ordinary-ready queries, while a readiness-maximizing oracle yields 286, including 32 wrong-schema-ready cases. Among tested heuristic rules, the largest observed readiness count is 282, with 20 schema regressions.
after: Oracle A selects the gold schema whenever it occurs in the top ten, otherwise retaining the baseline: it yields 268/331 ordinary-ready queries and 325/331 correct schemas. Oracle C selects the gold schema only when its grounding is ready, otherwise retaining the baseline: it yields 270/331 ordinary-ready queries and 322/331 correct schemas. Its ready set includes two wrong-schema cases, \path{nlp4lp_test_286} and \path{nlp4lp_test_299}. Their gold candidates, at ranks four and six, have coverage $2/3$ and $1/2$ and fail readiness; oracle A switches to them, whereas C retains the wrong but ready baseline choices. Thus both oracles have 268 schema-correct ready queries. Oracle B maximizes readiness within the top ten without requiring the correct schema and yields 286 ready queries, including 32 wrong-schema-ready cases. Among tested heuristics, the top-five readiness-first rule yields the largest observed readiness count, 282, with 20 schema regressions.

before: Compatibility and validity checks also differ from semantic validation.
after:
Refai and Ahmed evaluate generated formulations at the component level, including decision-variable and constraint precision/recall and constraint/objective root mean squared error \cite{refai2026component}. OPT-Engine varies optimization-problem complexity to diagnose formulation and solving limitations, including constraint formulation \cite{chen2026optengine}. These works share our diagnostic motivation. Here, complete stored-reference agreement is conditioned on readiness in a reference-assisted scalar inventory; ordered gate accounting and fixed-score decoder comparisons delimit the failures and attributions supported by that setting.

OptMATH synthesizes modeling data through back-translation and forward checking \cite{lu2025optmath}; our external extraction check does not evaluate that synthesis framework or full-pipeline transfer. Autoformulation combines LLM-guided Monte Carlo tree search with symbolic pruning over formulations \cite{astorga2025autoformulation}. Its search space includes modeling decisions absent from our supplied-slot assignment controls. These task distinctions do not constitute empirical comparisons with either system.

Compatibility and validity checks also differ from semantic validation.
